What number is missing from the boxes in the statement below?

The ratio of heptagons to squares is $1:\boxed{}\,$ because there is $1$ heptagon for every $\boxed{}$ squares.
question.worked_solution:
First, we count the number of heptagons. We see that there are $4$ heptagons.

Then, we count the number of squares. We see that there are $4$ squares.

So the ratio of heptagons to squares is $4:4.$

We can simplify this ratio by dividing both numbers by $4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,4 &  & : & \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,4 &  \\ \,\,↓÷\,\,4 &  &  &  & \,\,\,↓÷\,\,4 &  \\ \,\,1 &  & : &  & \,\,\,1 & \end{aligned}
$$

This means that $1:1$ is equivalent to $4:4.$ 

So, the complete statement is
"The ratio of heptagons to squares is $1:1$ because there is $1$ heptagon for every $1$ square."
